props.title: Raw Deal
props.initialSlug: Ex-FBI agent fights mob to avenge partner's death

sections.content: **Raw Deal** (1986) sits at a fascinating intersection of 1980s action cinema, coming during Arnold Schwarzenegger's meteoric rise between **The Terminator** (1984) and **Predator** (1987). Director John Irvin delivers a gritty crime thriller that lets Arnold flex both his action chops and surprising dramatic range as a former FBI agent going undercover in the mob. While not as widely celebrated as **Commando** (1985) or **The Running Man** (1987), Raw Deal showcases the evolution of 80s action from stripped-down violence toward more complex plotting, though still anchored by explosive set pieces and quotable one-liners.

sections.content: The film's positioning in the crime thriller genre reveals interesting parallels with other 1980s undercover cop films like **To Live and Die in L.A.** (1985) and **52 Pick-Up** (1986). While those films leaned harder into neo-noir territory, Raw Deal maintains a foot in both worlds - mixing moody criminal intrigue with Schwarzenegger's emerging larger-than-life action hero persona. The film's violence and style clearly influenced later undercover thrillers like **Point Break** (1991) and **Donnie Brasco** (1997).

Director John Irvin, fresh off the acclaimed war film **The Dogs of War** (1980), brings a grittier European sensibility to the material. This creates an interesting tension with Schwarzenegger's more bombastic elements, prefiguring how directors like John McTiernan would later blend serious action filmmaking with larger-than-life heroes in films like **Die Hard** (1988). The Chicago mob setting also connects Raw Deal to a broader 1980s trend of action films using organized crime as a backdrop, seen in everything from **Code of Silence** (1985) to **Above the Law** (1988). sections.content: Raw Deal marks an important step in Schwarzenegger's transformation from pure muscle-bound star to more nuanced action hero. While still delivering the expected one-liners and explosive action, his character Mark Kaminsky shows more emotional depth than earlier roles. This character development would continue through films like **Predator** (1987) and **Total Recall** (1990), where Arnold proved increasingly capable of carrying both dramatic weight and action sequences. The film also demonstrates the growing sophistication of 1980s action cinema, as straightforward revenge plots began incorporating more complex narratives about corruption and morality.
